original_question: Does there exist a connected compact group G for which ms_r(G) < 1/r^2 for some integer r? In particular, what are the exact values of ms_2(SO(3)) and of ms_2(S^3), where S^3 is the multiplicative group of unit quaternions?
target_in_paper: Question 7.11 in Section 7, concerning maximal symmetry numbers of connected compact topological groups under central symmetries and, specifically, the cases SO(3) and S^3.
correct_elements: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. It correctly captures the existential question about a connected compact group G with ms_r(G)<1/r^2 for some integer r, and it correctly singles out the two concrete special cases asked in the paper: ms_2(SO(3)) and ms_2(S^3), with S^3 viewed as the multiplicative group of unit quaternions.
missing_details: G should be specified as a connected compact topological group, equipped with its normalized Haar probability measure.
The notation ms_r(G) should be defined explicitly as the paper’s maximal symmetry number for the symmetry measure space attached to G.
The admissible symmetries are the central symmetries of G, namely the involutions s_c:G→G given by s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c for c∈G.
The colorings in the definition are measurable r-colorings (equivalently, measurable partitions into r color classes), not arbitrary set-theoretic colorings.
A subset is 'symmetric' here only in the paper’s sense: A is s_c-symmetric for some c∈G, i.e. s_c(A)=A.

The quantifier in the definition of ms_r(G) is over all measurable r-colorings, and ms_r(G) is the largest real ε such that every such coloring contains a monochromatic measurable symmetric subset of Haar measure at least ε.
r should be stated as a positive integer.
S^3 should be identified explicitly as the multiplicative group of unit quaternions.
refined_question: Let G be a connected compact topological group, endowed with its normalized Haar probability measure μ and the family of central symmetries s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c (c∈G). For a positive integer r, let ms_r(G) denote the maximal symmetry number of G, i.e. the largest ε∈[0,1] such that every measurable r-coloring of G contains a monochromatic measurable subset A with μ(A)≥ε and s_c(A)=A for some c∈G. Does there exist a connected compact topological group G and some r∈N such that ms_r(G)<1/r^2? In particular, what are the exact values of ms_2(SO(3)) and ms_2(S^3), where S^3 is the multiplicative group of unit quaternions?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since each central symmetry s_c is involutive, is there a connected compact topological group G and some r∈N for which one can find a measurable r-coloring G=A_1∪⋯∪A_r such that μ(A_i∩s_c(A_i))<1/r^2 for every color class A_i and every c∈G? In particular, determine the optimal such bound for G=SO(3) and G=S^3.
justification: The nearest official target is Question 7.11, stated immediately after Theorems 7.9 and 7.10 in Section 7. The threshold 1/r^2 is not an invention of the draft; it is the exact benchmark around which the paper formulates the open problem, motivated by the lower-bound results in Theorems 7.9 and 7.10. The surrounding Section 7 context supplies the group-specific setup: compact topological groups are endowed with Haar measure and the family of central symmetries, and ms_r(G) denotes the resulting maximal symmetry number. Section 3 gives the general definition of maximal symmetry numbers in symmetry measure spaces and the involutive reformulation used here. So the draft is essentially correct but needs the measurable/Haar/symmetry setup to be fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
